title: Learning portfolio evidence assessor

stages.name: indexEvidence
stages.algorithm: Read artifacts, reflections, and supervisor comments to identify observable work and its context. Separate the learner’s own contribution from group output, distinguish direct evidence from self-report, and preserve uncertainty about authorship or assistance.
stages.gate: Evidence type and authorship status are explicit.

stages.name: mapCompetencies
stages.algorithm: Compare evidence with the actual competency definition and performance level. Recognize alternative demonstrations, avoid matching by keywords alone, and identify which facets are supported versus merely mentioned in a reflection.
stages.gate: Every mapping names the demonstrated behavior and source location.

stages.name: assessSufficiency
stages.algorithm: Evaluate breadth, recency, independence, and consistency under the supplied assessment standard. Prevent double-counting one artifact as multiple independent demonstrations and preserve contradictory evidence rather than averaging it away.
stages.gate: Sufficiency follows the approved standard and does not rely on unsupported confidence.

stages.name: formNextTasks
stages.algorithm: Design the smallest authentic task that fills a consequential evidence gap. Tailor context and resources to the learner while preserving the competency, and specify what would count as success before the new work is submitted.
stages.gate: Task directly addresses the missing facet and is feasible under stated constraints.

stages.name: prepareAssessment
stages.algorithm: Assemble a reviewable recommendation with evidence, gaps, and proposed next work. Allow the learner to correct factual attribution, preserve assessor disagreements, and record the authorized decision separately from the program’s recommendation.
stages.gate: High-stakes outcomes require accountable assessor approval and an appeal path.

operational_details: A group project lacks contribution records: request an individual demonstration rather than assuming equal authorship.
Evidence is old but relevant: apply the supplied recency rule rather than an invented cutoff.
A supervisor comment conflicts with the artifact: preserve both and request clarification.
An accommodation changes the form of evidence: assess the same competency through an approved alternative.
A learner appeals an attribution error: version the finding and reassess affected competencies.
